newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt sentences seven to 10-25 years in prison.
newsitem.headline: Egypt sentences seven to 10-25 years in prison.

text.p: An Egyptian military court on Tuesday sentenced five Egyptians and two Sudanese to between 10 and 25 years in jail with hard labour for smuggling weapons and ammunition from Sudan, security sources said.
The court in the southern province of Assiut acquitted three Egyptians, the sources said.
Four defendants, all at large and including the two Sudanese, were sentenced to 25 years in prison. Two were sentenced to 15 years and one to ten years, they added.
The sources said the men smuggled 46 Kalashnikov rifles and more than five thousands rounds across the border earlier this year. The army said the defendants had planned to sell the arms in Egypt.
Border guards seized the cache in August in Qena province, 450 km (280 miles) south of Cairo.
The men were tried in a military court because they were arrested by the military's border guards.
Military courts have over the past few years tried civilians who were charged with belonging to militant groups trying to overthrow the Egyptian government.
